items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training
Experience working in higher education or a similarly complex organization.
Experience coordinating or supporting complex employee and labor relations matters, including policy interpretation, corrective action, grievances, and management consultation.
Extensive HR experience, including employee relations, classification, recruitment, compensation, documentation, performance management, and leaves of absence.
Experience implementing HR processes, protocols, and procedures in a complex organization.
Supervisory, managerial, or lead experience recruiting, training, evaluating, coaching, motivating, and managing staff performance.
Experience partnering with leadership, managers, employees, Academic HR, Human Resources partners, and campus or health system stakeholders.
Financial management experience related to total compensation and payroll.
Experience with university systems including UCPath, Ecotime, RECRUIT, OATS, APHID, AggieService, JobBuilder, iGlobal, and Handshake.

The Academic HR Supervisor supervises HR staff and administers assigned human resources programs and processes for the Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine, supporting personnel actions, HR compliance, workforce coordination, and related operational needs in consultation with department leadership and in alignment with University requirements.
20% - Workforce Management
10% - Budget and Accounting
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and HR, academic, and payroll systems.
Broad HR knowledge across employee relations, classification, recruitment, compensation, documentation, performance management, and leaves of absence.
Advanced knowledge of state and federal labor and employment laws, UC policies and procedures, and applicable contracts.
Ability to advise leaders, managers, supervisors, and employees on HR policy, procedure, collective bargaining agreements, employment law, and sensitive employee or labor relations matters.
Highly developed leadership, coaching, change management, political acumen, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, judgment, and decision-making skills, including the ability to gather and interpret data, identify trends, draw conclusions, and recommend practical solutions.
Workforce planning, program support, project coordination, and process improvement skills in a complex organization.
Advanced interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills, including writing, editing, proofreading, presentations, and consultation with diverse audiences.
Ability to handle confidential, sensitive, difficult, and crisis situations with diplomacy, tact, objectivity, and discretion.
Organizational skills to manage competing priorities, multiple projects, deadlines, interruptions, meetings, training sessions, and special events.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with individuals from diverse cultural, educational, and professional backgrounds.
